title: The 5 Heaviest Birds Alive, Ranked (One Lives on Antarctic Ice)

scenes.text: The five heaviest birds alive. One of them lives on the Antarctic ice.
Number five: the greater rhea of South America. About 23 kilos, and the male alone hatches and raises dozens of chicks at once.
scenes.label: Greater rhea · 23 kg

scenes.text: Number four: the emperor penguin. Around 31 kilos, up to 45 before the breeding fast, standing on ice at minus 40.
scenes.label: Emperor penguin · 31 kg

scenes.text: Number three: the emu. About 33 kilos and nearly two metres tall, running at 50 kilometres an hour across Australia.
scenes.label: Emu · 33 kg

scenes.text: Number two: the southern cassowary. Around 45 kilos, females up to 58, with a 12-centimetre dagger claw on each foot.
scenes.label: Cassowary · 45 kg

scenes.text: Number one: the common ostrich. About 104 kilos, up to 150, nearly three metres tall. Not one bird on this list can fly.
scenes.label: Ostrich · 104 kg

description:
The five heaviest living birds, ranked by average adult body mass.
The common ostrich averages about 104 kg (big males reach 150 kg) and stands up to 2.8 m; the southern cassowary about 45 kg (females to 58 kg); the emu about 33 kg; the emperor penguin about 31 kg (up to 45 kg before the winter fast); and the greater rhea about 23 kg. The Somali ostrich and northern cassowary are close sister species of numbers one and two. Every bird on the list is flightless.
Which one did you expect at number one, and what should we rank next?
first_comment: A penguin outweighs the greater rhea, and the ostrich outweighs the cassowary and the emu put together. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
